0.0.n: 失敗する describes the study method as one that leads to failure.

0.1.n: Combines with 方法 to specify what kind of method is being discussed.

0.2.n: 勉強方法 means a method of studying.

0.3.n: Combines with つ and 目 to identify the second item.

0.4.n: A general counting ending; 2つ is read ふたつ.

0.5.n: Added after a count, 目 marks position in a sequence rather than quantity.

0.7.n: This emphatic expression suggests including things indiscriminately, without exceptions.

0.8.n: Pairs with 一句 in the fixed expression 一語一句, emphasizing every detail of the wording.

0.9.n: Completes 一語一句, which describes translating without skipping any wording.

0.10.n: 翻訳しよう is the intention form of 翻訳する; adding とする expresses an attempt.

0.11.n: Links the intention form 翻訳しよう to する, creating the pattern for trying to do something.

0.12.n: Completes 翻訳しようとする; the whole phrase describes attempting translation.

1.0.n: Introduces the basic premise behind the speaker's argument.

1.1.n: A personal pronoun commonly used by male speakers; here たち expands it to a group.

1.2.n: Added to 僕 to make 僕たち, referring to the speaker and others together.

1.3.n: Marks 僕たち as the topic: the people whose language use is being discussed.

1.5.n: Combines with か to refer to an unspecified thing.

1.6.n: After 何, か creates 何か; it does not mark a question here.

1.7.n: 言う becomes 言いたい with たい, which expresses desire.

1.8.n: Turns 言いたい into a noun phrase referring to the content someone wants to express.

1.9.n: Marks 言いたいこと as what exists in the phrase with あった.

1.10.n: Past form of ある; before 時, it describes having something to say, not necessarily a past event.

1.11.n: The preceding phrase describes the situation in which communication happens.

1.12.n: After 時, に marks the time or occasion of the action.

1.14.n: Refers to language generally as a tool for communication.

1.15.n: Marks 言語 as what people use.

1.16.n: The て-form of 使う connects using language to conveying a message.

1.17.n: Refers to the person receiving the message, not an opponent here.

1.18.n: Marks 相手 as the recipient of what is conveyed.

1.19.n: Describes actively communicating something to someone; the message is understood from context.

1.20.n: Short for の; adds an explanatory tone before です.

1.21.n: Makes the explanation polite as part of んです.

1.22.n: Adds emphasis, presenting the explanation as something the listener should notice.

2.0.n: Together with ので, this forms a polite connector pointing back to the previous explanation.

2.1.n: In ですので, links the previous point to the conclusion that follows.

2.3.n: Signals a hypothetical situation, reinforced by the later あったら.

2.4.n: A borrowed word written in katakana, introduced as a hypothetical communication method.

2.5.n: Presents telepathy as one possible example rather than the only possibility.

2.6.n: The たら conditional form of ある imagines something existing.

2.8.n: 言う takes たい to express desire and describes the following こと.

2.9.n: Makes 言いたい into a noun phrase referring to the intended message.

2.10.n: Marks 言いたいこと as the message that would get across.

2.11.n: Suggests the intended message passes across unchanged, without conversion into language.

2.12.n: Unlike 伝える, this focuses on the message reaching someone rather than someone actively conveying it.

2.13.n: Introduces the reason language would be unnecessary.

2.15.n: Refers generally to the communication tool discussed in the previous line.

2.16.n: Casually includes language and similar tools, downplaying their necessity in this hypothetical situation.

2.17.n: Negative form of 要る, meaning to need, not いる meaning to exist.

2.18.n: Short for の; frames the conclusion as an explanation.

2.19.n: Adds politeness to the plain negative いらない through んです.

2.20.n: Emphasizes the conclusion for the listener.

0.lit: Study method that fails, second one: trying to translate absolutely everything, every word, every phrase.
0.tip: A verb's intention form followed by とする means trying to do something: 翻訳しようとする.

1.lit: To begin with, we, when we have something we want to say, use language and convey it to the other person.
1.tip: 言いたいこと means what someone wants to say; こと turns the preceding description into a thing being discussed.

2.lit: So, if telepathy or something existed, what we want to say would get across unchanged, so language would be unnecessary.
2.tip: 伝わる means a message gets across, while 伝える means someone actively conveys it.
